Work context
Ram is a trainer and course developer at Quality Thought, a tech upskilling company based in Hyderabad, India. His work centers on building educational content for tech professionals, with a current focus on Gen AI and Agentic AI testing curriculum. He also does work connected to Ramanasoft, an organization with a broader product ecosystem.
Personal context
Ram is based in Hyderabad and creates training content grounded in Indian cultural context, frequently using cricket and food analogies to make technical concepts accessible to local audiences.
Top of mind
Ram is deep in building a comprehensive Gen AI and Agentic AI Testing educational ecosystem at Quality Thought, including a 24-week course curriculum split into manual and automation streams targeting manual testers transitioning to AI testing specialists. Recent work has produced detailed trainer materials, professional presentations, capstone projects (AI Trip Planner with a full test suite), agent automation workshop packages, and multi-agent test case documentation across eight agent modules.
Brief history
Recent months
Ram has been prolific across several interconnected content and curriculum projects. For Quality Thought's Gen AI Testing course, he developed a full 24-week dual-stream curriculum, week-by-week trainer scripts, PIL-generated diagrams, real-world case studies (e.g., Cohen v. Avianca, NHS chatbot, Amazon hiring bias), and grading rubrics. Presentation work has been iterative — Ram prefers professional, layout-disciplined slides with no overlapping elements, rebuilt until meeting strict visual standards. Capstone and workshop deliverables include a stdlib-only Python API server, self-contained test suites, DeepEval and RAGAS evaluation suites, Playwright UI tests, Postman collections, and one-click run scripts for multiple OS platforms. He also produced a 50-test-case document for a multi-agent travel system covering orchestration, search, booking, payment, memory, and safety filter agents.
Separately, Ram developed an 8-slide presentation for Ramanasoft's 24-week internship program covering four phases (induction, core tools, frontend/backend dev, client deployment), referencing tools like GitHub, JIRA, and Agile/Scrum methodology.
For college outreach, Ram had a 14-slide partnership presentation built for Quality Thought covering an 8-semester engineering curriculum, certifications (including TCS iON, Infosys Springboard, Wipro TalentNext), hackathons, placement support, and a 200+ hiring partner network.
He also requested social media infographic sets (Instagram/Facebook) for a 3-day Gen AI Testing workshop, preferring clean white/light aesthetics with per-day color accents.
Earlier context
Ram developed 5-day Gen AI Testing training handouts in Word, PDF, and PowerPoint formats for tech professionals, structured around cricket and food analogies. Content spanned Gen AI foundations, prompt engineering (3R Framework), RAGAS evaluation, safety/bias/red teaming, and CI/CD integration. He also explored data centre job roles and detailed job descriptions for mid-experience candidates.
Interaction preferences
Ram communicates efficiently — often in shorthand or bullet notes — and expects Claude to interpret and expand inputs into polished, finished deliverables with minimal back-and-forth. He iterates through direct feedback rather than upfront detailed specs. Teaching materials are localized for Indian audiences, and he follows a portfolio-first learning model where every course week produces a named GitHub artifact.

The best time to visit Bali is during the dry season, from April to October, when the weather is sunny with low humidity.
The wet season runs from November to March and brings frequent rain.
Popular attractions include Ubud's rice terraces, Uluwatu Temple, Seminyak beaches and Mount Batur for sunrise hikes.
Bali is generally safe for tourists. Take normal precautions with valuables and use licensed taxis.

Barceloneta beach is popular in summer.

Indian passport holders can obtain a visa on arrival in Thailand for tourism for a stay of up to 15 days.
The visa on arrival fee is 2000 Thai Baht and requires a passport valid for at least 6 months, a return ticket and proof of funds.
For stays longer than 15 days, Indian travellers should apply for a tourist visa at a Thai embassy or consulate before travelling.
Entry rules change frequently. Always confirm the current requirement with the official Thai embassy before you travel.
